tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: PRD Phase 1. assemblies-lite folded into B1 (engine/assemblies.py scaffolded). Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). The last pillar between us and estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Build the per-room assembly formulas that map classified room types (bedroom, bathroom, corridor) to measurable quantities — paint SF, drywall SF, flooring SF — for the estimator-grade Excel output.
prep.understand: The `engine/assemblies.py` scaffold exists from Phase 0 assemblies-lite. A 'room type' classification drives a set of assembly formulas (e.g., bedroom = paint SF from perimeter × height, flooring SF from area). CSI MasterFormat Division 09 (Finishes) is the industry convention for assembly categories. Wall heights come from the already-shipped `wall_height_ft` field, set via the engine's PATCH measurement route.
approach: Open `engine/assemblies.py` — review what's scaffolded vs still placeholder, and note the assembly dict shape
Define room-type → assembly mappings: bedroom/living room = paint (perimeter × height) + flooring (area); bathroom = tile + drywall; corridor = flooring + paint
Wire each formula to pull `wall_height_ft` and `area`/`perimeter` from the Measurement row
Extend `engine/excel.py` to emit the assembly quantities as a new tab, then run the gauntlet — all 81+ pins must stay bit-identical
resources: `engine/assemblies.py` (existing scaffold — start here)
`engine/excel.py` (existing 5-tab workbook builder to extend)
CSI MasterFormat Division 09 for assembly naming conventions
`pytest` suite — run `pytest service/` locally after each change
docs/PRD Phase 1 section (assembly quantity targets)

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on the Harborview demo: rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text (55 live words, zero room labels found). v2 = productize M3 tiles lane as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action + callout-vs-room filtering for noise like FEC/stair arrows.

prep.what: Fix the 'unnamed rooms' failure for PDFTron-outlined-text blueprints by productizing the M3 vision tiles lane as an opt-in 'Read labels (AI)' endpoint, plus add callout filtering so stair arrows and FEC codes stop matching as room names.
prep.understand: PDFTron renders text as vector outlines — `pdfplumber` finds ZERO readable characters on these sheets. The M3 tiles lane (`run_labels_m3tiles.py` spike) uses MiniMax AI vision to read outlined text; it works but costs ~$0.01/sheet and takes ~4.3 min, so it must be opt-in. Callout noise is a separate issue: holabird currently labels 'UP', 'FEC', and paragraph notes as room names. Both must be addressed to make the labels lane production-ready.
approach: Wire `run_labels_m3tiles.py` as a POST `/projects/{id}/labels/ai` endpoint with a metered-credits event (§7a) — async, same RQ worker pattern as the measure job
Add MINIMAX_AI key to VPS `.env` using the same chmod-600 / API_KEYS_RAW pattern; commit only the env-var NAME to docker-compose, never the value
Add callout-vs-room filtering: reject labels matching known non-room patterns ('UP', 'DN', 'FEC', strings > 40 chars, all-caps 3-letter codes)
Test end-to-end with the Harborview blueprint (the failing case) and confirm holabird still names 92/109 rooms
resources: `service/run_labels_m3tiles.py` (M3 spike to productize)
Harborview blueprint PDF (the failing demo case — use this to test)
docs/STATE.md R13 polish section (callout filtering context)
`/opt/takeoff-engine/.env` on the VPS (chmod 600, root — for MINIMAX_AI key)
MiniMax AI vision API docs (tiles endpoint parameters)

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add wall/ceiling height input (project default + optional per-room override); wall paint SF/room = perimeter x height. Emit a 'Wall paint area' line per room.

prep.what: Make painting auto-measurable from a takeoff blueprint by computing wall surface area (perimeter × height) per room — right now painting gets zero-area $0 lines because 2D plans have no Z-axis.
prep.understand: Blueprints are flat — no wall height exists in the file. `wall_height_ft` must come from the user (project-level default, optional per-room override). The takeoff ENGINE already stores `wall_height_ft` per measurement (PATCH route from takeoff-engine t28). The critical issue: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` currently DROPS geometry/perimeter from measurement data — that must change before perimeter × height is computable. Wall area is the only way Rafa measures painting jobs.
approach: Run `php artisan make:migration add_wall_height_ft_to_estimates` and add a nullable float column to `estimates`
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, stop discarding the `geometry` block — preserve `perimeter` from each measurement's response
Compute wall paint SF = perimeter × wall_height_ft per room and emit a `kind=material` 'Wall paint area' estimate line (use the painting trade)
Add a wall height input to `Takeoff/Index.vue` — a project-level default field (e.g., 9 ft), with a per-room override exposed on the room table row
resources: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` (find where geometry is dropped — fix it here)
`resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue` (add the wall height input UI)
Takeoff Engine API response shape — `measurements[].geometry.perimeter` is what you need
`php artisan make:migration` (start with this)
`WalkThroughEstimateSeeder.php` (reference for how estimate lines are assembled)

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into one anonymous kind=custom $0 line, dropping kind+geometry. Preserve+switch on kind: area(SF)->flooring, derived wall SF->painting, line(LF)->wall-linear/trim, count(EA)->doors/tile. Tag each line with a trade via the core-vs-subbed helper.

prep.what: Make the takeoff seeder route each measurement to the correct trade instead of dumping everything as anonymous zero-dollar custom lines — areas go to flooring, wall SF to painting, LF to trim, counts to doors/tile.
prep.understand: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` ignores measurement `kind` and creates one `kind=custom` $0 line for everything. The measurement API returns a `kind` field: `area` (square feet), `line` (linear feet), `count` (each). The `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` helper exists for trade tagging. Note: LF routing fully works only after t47 (PerLinearFt RateType) lands — but you can stub the unit as 'lf' string for now and wire it properly in t47.
approach: In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, add a `routeToTrade(string $kind): string` helper that switches on measurement kind → trade slug
For `area` kind: use `LineItemFactory::fromMaterial()` pattern with trade=flooring
For derived wall-SF (from t45): use trade=painting — this is why t45 should run today first
For `line` (LF) kind: create a trim line with unit='lf' (t47 will add the proper RateType); for `count` (EA): create a door/tile line
resources: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` (the file to refactor — routing switch goes here)
`app/Enums/ProjectType.php` (isCoreTrade() and group() — use for trade tagging)
`LineItemFactory.php` (fromMaterial, fromLaborRate patterns to follow)
Takeoff Engine API measurement kinds: `area`, `line`, `count` — confirm from a real /measurements response
`php artisan test --filter TakeoffEstimate` (run after each routing case)

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Add PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft' (+ label), wire LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType->'lf', seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before takeoff pricing.

prep.what: Add `per_linear_ft` to the RateType enum so trim lines have a real rate type, unit label, and seeded LaborRate — quick and contained, but everything downstream in t48 pricing depends on it.
prep.understand: The `RateType` enum drives how `LineItemFactory` prices and labels estimate lines (per_sqft → 'sqft', per_unit → 'ea', etc.). Right now there's no LF variant, so trim lines from t46 can't be properly priced. This task is three small files: the enum, the factory, and the seeder. The whole thing should take 20 minutes — the test run is the other 10.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to `app/Enums/RateType.php` with a label method returning 'Per Linear Foot'
Update `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` to return `'lf'` for the new case
Add a trim install LaborRate in `LaborRateSeeder.php` (trade=trim, rate_type=per_linear_ft, price ≈ $3.50/lf — adjust to Rafa's real rate later)
Run `php artisan db:seed --class=LaborRateSeeder` and `php artisan test --filter RateType` to confirm clean
resources: `app/Enums/RateType.php` (add the new case — follow the existing pattern)
`LineItemFactory.php` (unitFromRateType method — one line to add)
`LaborRateSeeder.php` (follow an existing row's shape for the new trim row)
`php artisan test --filter LaborRate` (run this to confirm no regression)
